standard_prerequisites.name: Kummer sequence and Artin-Schreier sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the short exact Kummer sequence for l invertible in K and the Artin-Schreier sequence in characteristic p

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the Brauer group of finite extensions (the hypothesis of the statement)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The hypothesis Br(K') = 0 for every finite extension K' of K, together with the identification of Br(K') with H^2 of the Galois group with coefficients in the multiplicative group
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the input that kills the second cohomology of the multiplicative group, hence the Brauer group, in the Kummer case.

core_obligations: Translate to etale cohomology (proof lines 10709-10729): set p = char(K) and use the comparison of Galois with etale cohomology, the identification of the Brauer group with H^2, and the description of sheaves on the spectrum of a field, to restate both assertions as vanishing statements about etale cohomology of Spec(K).

Case l different from p (proof lines 10732-10755): for an invertible prime l consider the Kummer sequence on Spec(K'), use the vanishing of the Brauer group of every finite extension to get H^2 = 0, and then propagate the vanishing to all q at least 1 by dimension shifting along the long exact sequence.

Case l equal to p (proof lines 10758-10776): in characteristic p use the Artin-Schreier sequence instead, whose long exact cohomology sequence and the vanishing of the first cohomology of the structure sheaf on a field give the vanishing for torsion coefficients, which together with the previous case gives assertion (2).

Assertion (1) (proof lines 10779-10794): with G = Gal(K^sep/K) and M = (K^sep)^*, the author shows the vanishing of H^q(G, M) for all q at least 1, using the exact sequence relating M to its divisible part and the vanishing already established.
proof_roadmap: Restate both vanishing statements as statements about etale cohomology of Spec(K).
For primes l invertible in K, use the Kummer sequence and the vanishing of the Brauer group of finite extensions, then dimension shift.
For l equal to the characteristic, use the Artin-Schreier sequence instead.
Finally prove the vanishing for the full multiplicative group by comparing it with its divisible part.
difficulty_reason: The proposition, attributed by the author to Serre, deduces the vanishing of Galois cohomology from the vanishing of the Brauer groups of all finite extensions of K: H^q(Gal(K^sep/K), (K^sep)^*) = 0 for q at least 1 and H^q(Gal, M) = 0 for torsion M and q at least 2 (statement lines 10693-10707, whose commented reference block is excluded from the counted spans as explained in the notes). The proof proceeds by translating to etale cohomology of Spec(K) (proof lines 10709-10729), then splits according to whether the prime l under consideration differs from or equals char(K): the Kummer sequence together with the hypothesis on Brauer groups and dimension shifting handles the first case (proof lines 10732-10755), the Artin-Schreier sequence handles the second (proof lines 10758-10776), and assertion (1) requires a further argument comparing the multiplicative group with its divisible part (proof lines 10779-10794). The non-formal content is the organisation of the two characteristic cases and the final dimension argument. The claim is H2: a complete author proof with three separate steps, each written out.
